Handover notes

Source: vignettes/articles/handover.Rmd
handover.Rmd

Written 2026-11-26. These notes are for whoever takes over the project. They describe how things are set up and how to work on them. For what has been found so far, and why, read the lab notebook, starting with its status table.

1. Where things stand

Aim. Estimate vaccine effectiveness as a function of time since vaccination, VE(t), using a Poisson approximation to a Cox model in which the baseline hazard is driven by an age-structured force of infection (FoI). The project started as Group D at the Lorentz Center workshop (June 2026).

What works.

  • The full pipeline, from raw vaccination and case records to a fitted VE(t) curve, is in the package, tested, and documented on the website.
  • On simulated data with a known VE(t), the model recovers the curve and distinguishes waning from no waning (lab notebook entry 7).

Known limitations (details in the lab notebook):

  • Time since vaccination is measured to the report date, not the infection date, so the estimate lags the truth (entry 7), and VE for the first 7 days is not estimable once early cases are censored (entry 12).
  • Late VE (90+ days) is underestimated in the waning scenario. About half of this comes from calendar time being confounded with time since vaccination (entry 9).
  • In the current simulations the FoI adds no precision, because vaccination is random with respect to exposure (entry 10).
  • HERMES vaccinates people who are infectious or recovered, which ends their infection or removes their natural immunity (entry 11). This is kept deliberately, because real campaigns vaccinate them too; the analysis censors them instead (entry 12).

2. Where everything lives

What Where
This package: code, data, Stan models, tests, website, lab notebook GitHub kylieainslie/surviver (public, branch main)
HERMES simulator with the waning-VE extension GitHub kylieainslie/ibm_hermes, branch waning-vaccine-effectiveness. A fork of lwillem/ibm_hermes (Lander Willem); our changes are not upstream. The model is described in the HERMES user manual
Workshop record: original scripts, case-study data (200,000 people), the first Group D vignettes GitHub kylieainslie/lorentz_center_workshop, branch group-D, analysis/group-D/ and data/. Kept as a historical record; not developed further
Website https://kylieainslie.github.io/surviver/, rebuilt automatically on every push to main

3. Setting up 

# 1. Clone both repositories (shell):
#    git clone https://github.com/kylieainslie/surviver.git
#    git clone -b waning-vaccine-effectiveness https://github.com/kylieainslie/ibm_hermes.git

# 2. R packages (from the surviver folder)
install.packages(c("devtools", "pak"))
pak::local_install_dev_deps()       # Imports + Suggests, incl. cmdstanr from GitHub

# 3. CmdStan, for fitting
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()

# 4. Tell surviver where HERMES is, if not at ~/Documents/ibm_hermes.
#    Add to ~/.Renviron:   HERMES_PATH=/path/to/ibm_hermes

# 5. Check everything works
devtools::test()
devtools::check()

Versions used so far: R 4.5.2, CmdStan 2.39.0. fit_ve() caches the compiled Stan model in tools::R_user_dir("surviver", "cache"); delete that folder if a model seems stale after editing a .stan file.

HERMES itself is not an R package. Its scripts source() each other with paths relative to the repository root, so always load it from that folder:

hermes <- new.env()
withr::with_dir(Sys.getenv("HERMES_PATH", "~/Documents/ibm_hermes"), {
  sys.source("lib/ibm_core.R", envir = hermes)
  sys.source("lib/ibm_waning_scenario.R", envir = hermes)
})

4. Working conventions

  • Lab notebook. Every check or validation run gets a dated entry in vignettes/articles/lab-notebook.Rmd with question, method, results as observed, conclusion, and next step, plus a script in dev/checks/. Save figures to vignettes/articles/figures/ with the same date prefix. Never edit past results; add a new entry or a dated note. Update the status table and timeline at the top.
  • Check scripts run from the package root, load the package with devtools::load_all(), and write outputs to $SURVIVER_CHECKS_OUT (default: a temporary folder).
  • Website. Pushing to main rebuilds it. To preview locally: pkgdown::build_site() and open docs/index.html (docs/ is git-ignored).
  • Standard analysis. Censor people reported within 7 days of vaccination (counting_process(pop, censor_at_vaccination = reported_soon_after_vaccination(pop, 7))) and report VE from day 7 (lab notebook entry 12). For real data, choose the window from published incubation and reporting-delay distributions.
  • Changes to HERMES go on the waning-vaccine-effectiveness branch of the fork. Commit before regenerating data, because each dataset records the HERMES commit it came from, and the data script warns if HERMES has uncommitted changes.

5. Regenerating the simulated datasets

The package datasets ve_sim_waning and ve_sim_no_waning come from data-raw/ve_test_scenarios.R:

# from the surviver folder
source("data-raw/ve_test_scenarios.R")   # about 20 s per scenario
devtools::document()
devtools::test()                         # tests/testthat/test-data.R checks structure

The script loads HERMES, calls simulate_waning_scenario() once with ve_floor = 0.1 and once with ve_floor = 0.8, drops HERMES-only columns, stores the HERMES commit in hermes_commit, and saves with usethis::use_data().

Precomputed fits. The “Get started” vignette shows fits loaded from inst/extdata/ve_fits.rds, because Stan cannot run during R CMD check or on GitHub Actions. Rerun source("data-raw/ve_fits.R") (about 2 minutes) after any change to the datasets, the Stan models or the standard analysis, then copy the VE figure from the rebuilt site (docs/articles/surviver_files/figure-html/fit-ve-1.png) to man/figures/README-ve-fit.png.

Reproducibility. Every random step in the scenario is seeded from rng_seed (default 2026), including reporting. The current datasets were made with HERMES commit 6c9ab73; later commits on the branch reproduce them exactly. If a regenerated dataset changes, record that in the lab notebook, because earlier entries’ numbers refer to the old data.

Getting what the datasets leave out. The exported tables only contain what an analyst would see. HERMES keeps the full state of every person (true infection time, symptom onset, death, …). Run with a known output_dir and read the final snapshot:

sc  <- hermes$simulate_waning_scenario(ve_floor = 0.1, output_dir = "out/waning")
full <- readRDS("out/waning/pop_data_intervention16.rds")   # 16 = n_chunks
full$ind_id <- rownames(full)
# columns include time_of_infection, time_of_symptom_onset, health,
# time_of_vaccination, time_of_death, infector_id, ...

Snapshots after each vaccination round are pop_data_intervention1.rds … pop_data_interventionN.rds. Lab notebook entries 8, 11 and 12 use these.

6. Adapting the simulations

Changing scenario settings

simulate_waning_scenario() (HERMES lib/ibm_waning_scenario.R) takes:

Argument Default Meaning
ve_floor 0.1 Long-run VE after waning; set equal to vaccine_effectiveness for no waning
vaccine_effectiveness 0.8 Peak VE
ve_ramp_days 14 Days to reach peak VE
ve_half_life 45 Half-life of the waning, in days
pop_size 10,000 Population size (runtime grows with it; 100,000 has not been timed)
transmission_prob 0.02 Per-contact transmission probability. Chosen so the epidemic lasts the whole study; see lab notebook entry 2 before changing it
num_infected_seeds 10 Initial infections
initial_days 20 Days before vaccination starts
n_chunks, chunk_days 16, 10 Number and length of vaccination rounds; study length is initial_days + n_chunks * chunk_days
chunk_coverage 0.03 Share of the eligible population vaccinated per round
rng_seed 2026 Seed for all random steps
output_dir temporary Where HERMES writes its snapshots

Other HERMES parameters (contact probabilities, natural history, reporting delay) are set in lib/ibm_parameters.R (get_default_parameters()) and lib/ibm_delay_parameters.R. Changing those defaults affects every HERMES scenario, so prefer setting them inside the scenario function.

Using a new scenario without adding it to the package 

sc <- hermes$simulate_waning_scenario(ve_floor = 0.3, ve_half_life = 90)
sim <- list(
  demographic = sc$demographic_data,
  vaccination = sc$vaccination_data,
  incidence   = sc$incidence_data_reduced,
  params      = sc$params,
  study_end   = sc$study_end
)
pop <- ve_population(sim)        # then the usual pipeline (see README)
truth <- true_ve(1:160, sim$params)

Alternatively, hermes$export_waning_scenario(sc, "some/folder") writes the four .rds files, and ve_population("some/folder") reads them.

Adding a new scenario to the package

  1. Add a call in data-raw/ve_test_scenarios.R (or a new data-raw/ script) and include it in usethis::use_data().
  2. Document it in R/data.R and run devtools::document().
  3. Extend tests/testthat/test-data.R.
  4. Add a lab-notebook entry describing it, like entry 5.

Replicate simulations

Use different rng_seed values. Each seed changes the synthetic population as well as the epidemic, and epidemic size varies a lot between seeds (seed 7 gave 1,156 reported cases against 1,566 for seed 2026), so record the number of cases among vaccinated people per replicate. A sketch:

run_one <- function(seed, ve_floor) {
  sc  <- hermes$simulate_waning_scenario(ve_floor = ve_floor, rng_seed = seed)
  sim <- list(demographic = sc$demographic_data, vaccination = sc$vaccination_data,
              incidence = sc$incidence_data_reduced, params = sc$params,
              study_end = sc$study_end)
  pop  <- ve_population(sim)
  prev <- daily_prevalence(daily_incidence(pop))
  foi  <- force_of_infection(prev, age_group_sizes(pop))
  cp   <- counting_process(pop, censor_at_vaccination =
                             reported_soon_after_vaccination(pop, 7))
  sd   <- make_stan_data(expand_person_days(cp), foi)
  ve   <- extract_ve(fit_ve(sd, seed = seed, refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE))
  ve$truth <- true_ve(ve$days_since_vax, sim$params)
  ve$seed  <- seed
  ve
}
# about 20 s simulation + 40 s fit per replicate

Summarise bias (median − truth), coverage of the 90% interval and interval width by range of days since vaccination. The piecewise GLM in dev/checks/2026-11-25_03_calendar_time.R takes seconds and is a useful quick screen before running Stan on every replicate.

Changing how HERMES vaccinates

Vaccination happens at the start of each rerun_ibm() call in lib/ibm_core.R (look for is_eligible):

is_eligible <- which(pop_data$health != states$V & pop_data$health != states$D)
id_vaccinated <- sample(is_eligible, round(length(is_eligible) * params$vaccine_coverage, 0))
pop_data$health[id_vaccinated] <- states$V
pop_data$time_of_vaccination[id_vaccinated] <- nprev_days
  • Vaccinating infectious and recovered people is kept on purpose, because real campaigns do this too (decided 2026-11-26; lab notebook entries 11 and 12). The analysis censors them instead. If you ever want recovered people to keep their immunity, record time_of_vaccination for state R but leave health as R.
  • Targeted vaccination (e.g. oldest first): replace sample() with a selection that prioritises by pop_data$age. Add a new parameter (e.g. vaccine_priority = NULL) and keep the current random selection when it is NULL, so other scenarios are unchanged.

Changes to vaccination alter the simulated data, so regenerate the datasets and add a lab-notebook entry.

7. Where to go next

In rough order of priority. The lab notebook explains the reasons.

  1. Let transmission vary over calendar time in the model. Add a random walk on log_beta over calendar weeks (or days) to a new Stan model in inst/stan/, keeping the FoI offset. make_stan_data() already keeps day in its cells; pass a week index to Stan. Add the model name to ve_stan_file() and fit_ve(). Expected to remove the calendar-time part of the late underestimate (entry 9).
  2. Replicate simulations (above) to measure bias and coverage properly, including the choice of censoring window. Only then judge whether a frailty term is needed.
  3. Targeted-vaccination scenario, to test the project’s premise that the FoI improves VE estimation when exposure differs between vaccinated and unvaccinated people (entry 10).
  4. Frailty, if bias remains after 1–2. Note the model works on aggregated cells, so an individual random effect is not possible directly; a gamma frailty integrated out analytically (hazard divided by 1 + θ × cumulative hazard) can work at cell level.
  5. Delays between infection and reporting (entries 7 and 12). Options range from measuring time since vaccination to an estimated infection date to treating infection time as latent. This would also make the first week after vaccination estimable.
  6. Apply to the workshop case study (data/ in the workshop repository, read with ve_population("path/to/data")). Decide the value of theta first (entry 1 records the inconsistency).

8. Loose ends

  • HERMES reporting seed. get_default_delay_parameters() has no rng_seed, so reporting is unseeded in every HERMES run outside our scenario function (lab notebook entry 4). Worth reporting to Lander Willem (lwillem/ibm_hermes).
  • HERMES default parameters. Our branch changed package-wide defaults (waning VE, hospitalisation, mortality; entry 2). Revert these to the originals before proposing the branch upstream, and set them inside the scenario function instead.
  • Outdated documents. ibm_hermes/doc/vaccine_waning_vignette.Rmd still describes a 100,000-person scenario and old output paths, cites Young et al. 2018 as “Ferdinands et al.”, and understates how much longer HERMES’s incubation period is than published estimates (see lab notebook entry 2). The workshop repo’s data/ve_test_scenarios/ and its simulated-data vignette predate the reproducibility fix (entry 4); the package versions are the reference.
  • Stan prior on the first day. Both models put γ(1)∼N(−1,1)\gamma(1) \sim N(-1, 1), i.e. a prior centred on about 63% VE on the first day after vaccination. In the simulations VE starts at 0, so a prior centred at 0 may be more sensible. Not yet tested.
  • POLYMOD lookup. socialmixr warns that the automatic population lookup used in data-raw/polymod_nl.R is deprecated. The saved matrix is unaffected, but the script will need survey_pop in future versions.
  • Continuous integration. Only the website is built on GitHub. Consider adding usethis::use_github_action("check-standard") so tests run on every push.
